worked: Pennsylvania School Employees' Retirement System pension at 54, with a second job: item 5 has no age or retirement test. Federal AGI = wages person 0 30,000.00 + PA government pension person 0 36,000.00 = 66,000.00. Federal taxable income = 66,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 50,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 66,000.00; less 36,000.00 PA government pension person 0 (pa_public_pension); income after reliefs = 30,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 30,000.00. Tax = 30,000.00 x 0.0307 = 921.00. No credit in the projection; state income tax 921.00. Form: Line 1a/1c 30,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 30,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 30,000.00; Line 12 921.00. Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 30,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
